subject: Security exhibit: timeline approval, pen-test gates, and evidence ops playbook
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@helixhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureTeam <procure@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit + pen-test clause — initial asks

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Helix is excited to proceed. Before we finalize the MSA/order form, our security and procurement teams asked for two clarifications in the security exhibit:

1) Pen-test / forensic access: we prefer a 30-day notice window and a sampling limit (no more than 48 hours per staging host) — can Redwood accept explicit limits and an inspection carveout for customer-owned data?
2) SOC 2 evidence: due to our compliance timeline, we need an attestation or SOC2 report delivered within 10 business days of contract signature and a quarterly cadence for summary evidence.

I've attached our security checklist and a redline doc with suggested language. Can you confirm whether those asks are feasible operationally and legally? If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through redlines.

Thanks —
Ellen Park
Information Security Manager
Helix Health
Attachments: Helix_Security_Checklist_v1.pdf, Helix_MSA_requested_redlines.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Security exhibit + pen-test clause — initial asks

Looping you all in — Helix (Ellen) sent over the attached checklist and some proposed MSA redlines. Key asks from the external: 30-day pen-test notice + sampling limits, and SOC2 attestation/report within 10 business days of signature + quarterly evidence summaries.

Ask: can legal/infosec confirm acceptable language we can propose back? Ops (Jonas/Ben) — is the 30-day notice + limited sampling workable for staging access? Any runbook/contacts we should publish with the order form?

Proposed timeline (from my side):
- Today: internal redline comment return
- Tomorrow AM: propose consolidated language to Helix, ask them to confirm or book call
- 1 week: finalize order form redline and send to DocuSign

Attaching the Helix redlines and our SOC2 attestation (latest).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Helix_MSA_requested_redlines.docx, SOC2-attestation-2024.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Security exhibit + pen-test clause — initial asks

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the ping and Helix's redline. Quick legal read / recommendations:

- Pen-test language: we can accept a 30-day notice, but we should limit the scope to "non-production staging environments" unless Helix explicitly requests production inspection and signs an additional access addendum. Add a clause that testing requires prior written approval of testing scope and rollback plan.

- Sampling limits: rather than hard hours per host (which can be ambiguous), propose a sampling definition (e.g., "sampling of up to X% of instances or up to Y hosts per test, not to exceed N hours in aggregate"). Recommend: "sampling not to exceed 20% of staging hosts or 48 cumulative hours across the test window." This gives both sides clarity.

- SOC 2 evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II attestation within 10 business days of signature (we already have the attestation attached). For the quarterly cadence, propose delivering a "summary evidence pack" (control mapping and exception summary) quarterly; we should avoid delivering full underlying logs except via secured evidence transfers and with NDA/inspection request.

- Order form redlines: I'll attach a short redline with precise clause text (see attachment: MSA_exhibit_redline_LB_v1.docx). Key asks for Sales: get Helix to accept the staging carveout and the evidence cadence; if they insist on production testing or raw artifacts, we'll need a separate SOW and extra fees.

I can join the call tomorrow if needed — recommend we propose a 30-minute technical + legal sync with Helix.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_exhibit_redline_LB_v1.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 14:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Security exhibit + pen-test clause — initial asks

Marissa / team —

Operational note from infosec/ops perspective: Helix's asks are reasonable but we need to set explicit operational guardrails so support can meet the SLA. Proposed ops language:

- Pen-test window: 30-day notice is fine. We require a scoped test plan at least 10 business days before the test that includes target hosts, expected traffic profile, and rollback plan.
- Sampling limit: agree to 20% of staging hosts or up to 48 cumulative hours across the entire test window (this mirrors legal's suggestion).
- Evidence handoff cadence: we can deliver SOC2 attestation (PDF) within 10 business days. For the quarterly summary pack, we can publish a control-summary PDF and a change-log report (no raw logs).
- Runbook/access: we will provide a one-page "Inspection runbook" that lists contact names, procedures for ephemeral credentials, and the evidence request template. This will be an appendix referenced in the Order Form.

Notes / exceptions:
- If Helix requests production forensic access, that requires a separate SLA, approval from Security, and a signed SOW (extra fees).
- For staging access, we need Helix to confirm the environment host count and tagging (so we can calculate the 20% cap).

Jonas: can you confirm typical staging host counts for similar deals so we can recommend a numerical cap in the proposed language?

I can prepare the runbook draft and operational checklist to attach to the order form once we lock language.

Ben Carter
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@helixhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ProcureTeam <procure@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: timeline approval, pen-test gates, and evidence ops playbook

Marissa / Laura / Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposed language. Helix is OK with the staging carveout and the 20% / 48-hour cap as a starting point. Two follow-ups:

1) Host count: our staging environment is small (~30 hosts). Based on the 20% cap, that would allow testing of up to 6 hosts. That should work, but can Redwood confirm the calculation in the clause (we prefer the contract to say "up to X hosts based on the environment host count provided by the customer at time of test" so there's no ambiguity).
2) Evidence: Helix accepts SOC2 attestation within 10 business days and the quarterly summary pack. We do need the contact list and runbook ahead of signature so our security team can review procedures.

We are available for a 30-minute call Wednesday if folks want to hash final phrasing. Otherwise, we can confirm redlines in email and ask Procurement to circulate an updated order form for DocuSign.

Thanks —
Ellen Park
Information Security Manager
Helix Health
